signal_briefs.headline: Leonardo DRS Wins JIATF-401 Contract for Counter-UAS Capabilities
signal_briefs.summary: Leonardo DRS (DRS) won a $500M ceiling IDIQ with a three-year period of performance from JIATF-401 for counter-UAS rapid fielding, a direct contract win in the Physical AI / edge automation pillar. JIATF-401 is the joint interagency task force focused on illicit drone and weapons interdiction, so this validates DRS's counter-UAS sensor and EW portfolio as a priority end-user with repeat order flow. The ceiling is not guaranteed spend, but it removes the need to re-compete for three years and puts DRS ahead of smaller counter-UAS pure-plays for this buyer. signal_briefs.headline: Logical qubits start outperforming physical qubits - Quantinuum
signal_briefs.summary: Quantinuum's primary-source press release documents a logical-qubit error-correction milestone (real-time QEC fault-tolerant circuit entangling logical qubits, closing in on the QEC breakeven point). It is a genuine product milestone in the quantum pillar, but the release is dated August 2022 and is resurfacing, so it is not a fresh catalyst. The linked ticker QUBT is not Quantinuum (Quantinuum is private), so the mapping is weak and the item only supports a speculative read-through to the quantum complex. No direct revenue or contract fact for the tracked ticker.
signal_briefs.raw_text: Logical qubits start outperforming physical qubits Logical qubits start outperforming physical qubits Quantinuum closes in on breakeven point in quantum error correction August 4, 2022 ‍ Broomfield, Colorado, August 4 th , 2022 — Quantinuum researchers have hit a significant milestone by entangling logical qubits in a fault-tolerant circuit using real-time quantum error correction. The research, published in a new scientific paper that was released on August 3 rd , is the first experimental comparison study of different quantum error correction codes in similar environments and presents a collection of several different experiments. These experiments include: The first demonstration of entangling gates between two logical qubits done in a fully fault-tolerant manner using real-time error correction The first demonstration of a logical entangling circuit that has higher fidelity than the corresponding physical circuit. This milestone achievement is important because it marks the first time that logical qubits have been shown to outperform physical qubits — a critical step towards fault-tolerant quantum computers. “Quantinuum’s trapped-ion quantum computing roadmap is designed around continuous upgrades, enabled our flexible architecture and our precision control capabilities. signal_briefs.headline: Disclosed Defence Quantum Computing Money Doubled To Tripled
signal_briefs.summary: Aggregator analysis of disclosed DoD quantum money finds 2026 defense quantum spend roughly doubled-to-tripled vs the 2023-2025 average, driven almost entirely by two named DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative agreements: PsiQuantum's $125M expanded agreement (July 2026) and Diraq's $51M first tranche (Oct 7, 2026). The same Oct 7 event advanced IonQ, Atom Computing, IBM and Diraq to the QBI final stage with up-to-$300M ceilings — a concrete named-program milestone for IONQ. Rigetti's own QBI position was only a $1M first-stage completion award per its filing, so the pillar signal for RGTI is much weaker. Watch the distinction between ceilings and obligated money: register obligations actually fell in 2026.
signal_briefs.raw_text: Disclosed Defence Quantum Computing Money Doubled To Tripled Skip to content Illustration: Quantum Zeitgeist. Quantum Defence Disclosed defence money for quantum computing roughly doubled to tripled in 2026 against the 2023 to 2025 average, and all of the rise is announced money from two DARPA agreements. Obligated money on the federal register fell. Part of the rise may be more disclosure rather than more money. Defence money in quantum computing is easy to overstate. Headlines quote caps of $300 million and deals worth billions, but the money actually promised to named firms is far smaller than either. Counting priced awards on the register or announced by firms, defence buyers put $80 million into the field in 2023, $38 million in 2024 and $67 million in 2025. Then 2026 changed the scale. By 11 October the disclosed total stood at $157 million or $188 million, depending on whether PsiQuantum’s new agreement includes its earlier one. All of the rise is announced money from two DARPA agreements, with PsiQuantum and Diraq, while obligated money on the register fell from $35 million in 2025 to $12 million so far. Two more DARPA agreements that year carry no stated value, IBM’s place in the final stage of its test and a programme on mixing qubit types. IonQ’s and Atom Computing’s final-stage agreements state only the $300 million cap, which is counted as a ceiling. signal_briefs.headline: CACI Wins $500M Contract for SkyValor Drone Defense

IDIQ structure means follow-on task orders and force-wide follow-on awards (see NGC2 rollout context in the same feed) are the real expansion optionality. Watch for JIATF-401 option exercises and whether the Army/Navy counter-UAS buy lists add named SkyValor line items.

SkyValor detects, tracks and defeats hostile drones before they can threaten military operations. signal_briefs.headline: IonQ Wins AFRL Phase 2 Contract to Beam Quantum Entanglement Through Open Air Drones
signal_briefs.summary: IonQ secured a $7.5M AFRL Phase 2 contract to beam quantum entanglement through open air to drones, using quantum frequency converters to link different qubit types at the AFRL Rome, NY testbed. This is a named, government-issued contract with a concrete technical milestone (free-space entanglement delivery to airborne platforms) — squarely at the intersection of the quantum and Physical AI/counter-UAS pillars, and a step change from lab demos to fielded testbeds. Dollar size is small versus IONQ's market cap, so the revenue impact is low; the strategic value is the validated AFRL relationship and a Phase 3 pathway. Watch for follow-on Phase 3 award language and whether the converter IP extends to terrestrial nodes.
signal_briefs.raw_text: IonQ Wins AFRL Phase 2 Contract to Beam Quantum Entanglement Through Open Air to Drones Home Business Tech Money IonQ Wins AFRL Phase 2 Contract to Beam Quantum Entanglement Through Open Air to Drones Quantum Frequency Converters Will Link Different Qubit Types at AFRL’s Rome, New York Testbed By Edward Northmore Published: Oct 27 2026, 6:58 PM EDT Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share on Reddit Share on Flipboard Share on WhatsApp Ionq.com IonQ received $7.5 million in Phase 2 funding from the Air Force Research Laboratory to build quantum entanglement links that travel through open air rather than optical fiber — a step that, for the first time, makes quantum-secure communication with a moving drone or aircraft a concrete engineering program rather than a theoretical goal. The award, announced October 27, 2026, is contained within the original $21.1 million AFRL contract IonQ disclosed in January 2025 — not an addition to it — and represents a significant technical escalation from the fiber-based Phase 1 network already operational at the Innovare Advancement Center in Rome, New York. The shift from guided fiber to free space matters because fiber cables are fixed infrastructure. They can be cut, are expensive to deploy in contested environments, and have no path to a drone, a ship at sea, or a vehicle in the field. A free-space optical (FSO) quantum link, operating on tightly focused beams of light aimed by precision tracking hardware, can in principle connect a ground station to any mobile platform with a clear line of sight. "We are unlocking new domains for quantum networking by going to free space optics," said Jordan Shapiro, IonQ's President and General Manager of Quantum Networking. signal_briefs.headline: FormFactor sinks despite offering up strong Q3 results, guidance

For the semiconductors pillar, probe-card demand tracks wafer-start volumes at TSMC/Samsung advanced nodes, so the question is whether the stock move reflects a genuine demand roll-off signal or a liquidity/short-squeeze reversal. The gap between reported quality and price reaction is itself the signal: either insiders are fading the tape or the market is anticipating a Q4 mix shift.

signal_briefs.headline: Novel Crystal Technology Ships 150mm Ga2O3 Substrate Samples
signal_briefs.summary: Novel Crystal Technology (NCT, Sayama) began shipping 150mm (6-inch) beta-Ga2O3 (gallium oxide) substrate samples in March 2026, breaking the prior 100mm R&D ceiling — 150mm is the diameter standard production lines are built around, so this is a supply-chain scaling milestone for power-semiconductor substrates, not a lab curiosity. For the materials-science pillar, the power-semiconductor value chain is moving upstream from devices to substrates, and 150mm Ga2O3 opens a path to wafer-level cost parity for the next power-device generation. The tagged beneficiaries (AMKR, MTSI) are indirect: MTSI is a potential device-side adopter of Ga2O3 power tech while AMKR is exposed via the advanced-packaging/substrate ecosystem; neither is named as a customer. Direction is ambiguous — cheap 6-inch Ga2O3 substrates expand the TAM for device makers but also raise the competitive bar and could compress margins for incumbent wide-bandgap substrate suppliers.

Because this is an aggregator (StockTwits) price-mover piece, the downgrades are unnamed and unquantified, so confidence is low and the actual analyst targets are unknown. For MU specifically, the watch item is whether HBM-related guidance survives the China discount narrative at its next update.

signal_briefs.headline: AXT raises private equity financing of up to $545m in Tongmei
signal_briefs.summary: AXT (AXTI) says its majority-owned China-based wafer subsidiary Beijing Tongmei has signed definitive agreements for up to $545M in private equity financing to fund further manufacturing expansion of its GaAs, InP, and Ge substrate operations. The PE round removes the parent-level capital and dilution overhang that has capped AXTI's equity story and funds capacity expansion in substrates that sit on the AI optical interconnect (InP photonics) demand curve. Because the financing is at the subsidiary level, AXT's effective ownership in Tongmei will step down, so the benefit to AXTI shareholders is a function of retained stake and Tongmei's valuation at the close. China export-control and geopolitical exposure on the substrate business remain the structural risk. Watch the ownership math and any export-license conditions attached to Tongmei expansion.

signal_briefs.headline: EPC adds two three-phase inverter evaluation platforms to 100V GaN motor drive portfolio

These are developer-facing evaluation boards rather than revenue events, so near-term earnings impact is negligible; the value is deepening the design-in funnel for eGaN power conversion, which supports the broader edge robotics and motor-driven automation pillar. The 100V class targets higher-power motor drives, an area where eGaN is displacing Si and SiC in new designs. Incremental signal of portfolio breadth, not a catalyst-grade milestone. Watch for named design wins or customer announcements in the motor drive / robotics segment.

The work will combine engineering simulation with physical tests rather than rely on computer modeling alone. The collaboration is part of the Sustainable Tropical Data Centre Testbed Phase 2.0 (STDCT 2.0), hosted by the university’s College of Design and Engineering. Synopsys plans to contribute tools for modeling heat transfer and fluid flow, as well as technical expertise, training and research mentorship. Testing liquid cooling for high-density AI systems Higher-density racks built for AI accelerators produce substantial heat in a concentrated space. In Singapore, high ambient temperatures and humidity can make conventional cooling systems less efficient. Synopsys said cooling can account for as much as 40 percent of energy consumption in a tropical data center, an industry estimate that does not represent measured savings from this particular collaboration. Among the initial research topics is two-phase direct-to-chip cooling, in which a fluid absorbs heat near high-output computing components and changes phase during the process. Researchers intend to investigate how a design behaves under different loads and operating conditions before comparing model predictions with measurements from the testbed. Other planned activities include AI-assisted design studies and reduced-order models, which simplify detailed physics simulations so they can run faster in operational settings. signal_briefs.headline: DOE to invest $900M in next-generation nuclear
signal_briefs.summary: DOE's $900M appropriation for initial deployment of small modular reactor (SMR) technology is the anchor catalyst of the nuclear/SMR pillar. It is a named government investment that de-risks first-deployment capital — the single biggest hurdle for NuScale (SMR) — and sets a repeatable funding template for follow-on award rounds. For SMR this matters because reactor economics still hinge on who carries first-unit deployment risk, and a DOE-backed deployment mechanism shortens the path to first revenue and customer offtake. The ANS article is dated June 2024, so treat the figure as a program-level signal rather than a fresh, ticker-specific event and confirm it has not been superseded by a newer fiscal-year number before weighting it. Watch for which specific projects and named awards get carved out of the $900M.

signal_briefs.summary: The DOE selected five companies for advanced negotiations under the Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program (SPUP), which aims to convert surplus weapons-grade plutonium into reactor fuel — public start-ups Oklo (OKLO) and Flibe Energy (FLI) are among the five. Being named for advanced negotiations is a Tier-1 government program milestone for an advanced reactor pure-play: it ties the companies' fuel cycle directly to a federal stockpile-consumption mandate, a demand source private markets cannot replicate, and it removes a large regulatory overhang. For OKLO this is a direct, high-impact de-risking event for its SMR (small modular reactor) business case. Watch for the negotiation outcome and the terms (volume of plutonium, timeline).
signal_briefs.raw_text: DOE selects five companies to negotiate receipt of surplus U.S. plutonium -- ANS / Nuclear Newswire Fuel DOE selects five companies to negotiate receipt of surplus U.S. plutonium May 28, 2026, 12:29 pm Nuclear News Flibe Energy is one of five companies selected by the DOE for advanced negotiations under the Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program. (Image: Flibe) Nuclear start-ups Oklo and Flibe Energy both announced this week that they have been selected by the Department of Energy for advanced negotiations under the department’s Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program, which aims to make surplus U.S. plutonium available to the nuclear industry for advanced reactor fuels. According to multiple reports, three other companies—Exodys Energy, Shine Technologies, and Standard Nuclear—have also been selected for advanced negotiations under the program, which is being led by the DOE’s Office of Nuclear Energy. The program : The DOE established the Surplus Plutonium Utilization Program last year with a request for applications from prospective companies interested in receiving almost 20 metric tons of DOE-owned plutonium materials (4.4 MT metal and 15.3 MT oxides) for “recycling, processing, and manufacturing” into nuclear fuel for advanced reactors. The program follows President Trump’s Executive Order 14302, “Reinvigorating the Nuclear Base,” which ordered the DOE to halt its Biden-era “dilute and dispose program” and to “establish a program to dispose of surplus plutonium by processing and making it available to industry in a form that can be utilized for the fabrication of fuel for advanced nuclear technologies.” In 2024 , the DOE’s National Nuclear Security Administration issued a decision to dispose of up to 34 MT of surplus defense-related plutonium at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant in New Mexico using a “dilute-and-dispose” strategy. Also known as plutonium downblending, the strategy was adopted after the cancellation of the DOE’s mixed oxide (MOX) fuel project in 2018

signal_briefs.headline: Chemours Rolls Out Five-Fluid Faizeon Two-Phase Cooling Line for AI Data Centers
signal_briefs.summary: Chemours (CC/TWO) has rolled out a five-fluid Faizeon two-phase immersion/direct-to-chip cooling line aimed squarely at AI data centers. This is a concrete product-milestone expansion: it deepens their position in the thermal-dynamics pillar for AI data centers and differentiates against single-phase and air competitors. Cooler GPUs mean higher sustained power draw and density, a real selling point as AI racks push thermal limits. Watch for named customer design-ins and whether the five-fluid lineup expands to liquid immersion at scale.

Third-Party Tests Show 19-Degree GPU Advantage Over Water-Based Cooling That result anchors the company's case as it enters the two-phase liquid cooling market, where the physics of phase change, a fluid absorbing heat and converting from liquid to vapor, is used to pull high heat loads away from processors and server components. Systems engineered around Faizeon fluids, according to the company, can cut the energy consumed by data center cooling and, depending on system design and operating conditions, can nearly eliminate cooling-related water consumption. The fluids are also built for fluid circularity, meaning they can be recovered, reprocessed, and reused. Wilmington Chemical Company Unveils Portfolio Aimed at AI and HPC Heat The Chemours Company (NYSE: CC), headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware, announced the launch of the Faizeon two-phase liquid cooling portfolio on Nov. 2, 2026. The dielectric fluids are designed for artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and high-density data centers, spanning both two-phase direct-to-chip and two-phase immersion cooling. The company positions the lineup as giving data center operators and technology partners options that can accommodate evolving system architectures and remove heat from high-power processors and servers. The launch reflects a market dynamic the company describes plainly: as AI and HPC workloads push chip power and rack densities higher, cooling is increasingly becoming a critical constraint on data center infrastructure. This is a genuine technical milestone in the quantum pillar: logical-qubit scale is the gating metric for error-corrected machines, and hitting the published target validates the neutral-atom roadmap against rival ion-trap and superconducting approaches. Watch for error-rate data on the logical layer and any customer or government programs tied to the Sqale platform.
signal_briefs.raw_text: Infleqtion 30 Logical Qubits Rely on Error Detection Table of Contents September 24, 2026 – Infleqtion (NYSE: INFQ) said it had entangled 30 logical qubits encoded in 80 atoms on its Sqale neutral-atom quantum computer, meeting the logical-qubit target it had set for 2026. The company announced the result at Quantum World Congress 2026 and said the experiments were completed in August. Infleqtion builds neutral-atom quantum computers, optical clocks and quantum sensors. Its shares began trading on the New York Stock Exchange in February after it completed a business combination with Churchill Capital Corp X. The company said the new result made it the first neutral-atom quantum computing company to reach 30 logical qubits on a commercial system. In a technical post , Chief Technology Officer Pranav Gokhale said the team grouped the 80 atoms into 10 blocks of eight. Each block was prepared in the logical zero state of the distance-3 [[8,3,3]] code and then operated in the distance-2 [[8,3,2]] code, which Infleqtion said can detect any error or correct for a lost atom. Each block encodes three logical qubits. The test was an instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) circuit whose entangling gates, four logical controlled-controlled-Z (CCZ) gates among them, connected all 30 logical qubits. Infleqtion said the circuit placed all 30 in a single coherent state. The company said the circuit used 136 physical two-qubit gates and about 1,000 physical operations in total, an amount it called one KiloQuOp. Of the more than one billion possible 30-bit outputs, the ideal circuit produces 262,144, or one in 4,096. Infleqtion reported that about 25% of its measured outputs fell inside that set, roughly 1,000 times the rate that uniformly random outputs would achieve. The new portfolio includes dielectric fluids designed for both two-phase direct-to-chip and two-phase immersion cooling, helping data center operators manage high-power processors and servers from heating in evolving system architectures. The Faizeon fluids leverage phase-change technology, absorbing heat as the liquid converts into vapor to enable efficient heat removal. In independent third-party testing, a two-phase direct-to-chip system using Faizeon 200 maintained Graphics Processing Unit temperatures up to 19 degrees Celsius lower than a single-phase, water-based cooling system while requiring a lower coolant flow rate. The portfolio includes five products. Of these, Faizeon 100, 110, 200 and 220 are for direct-to-chip cooling, and Faizeon 500 is for full-server immersion cooling. These solutions are designed to deliver superior heat transfer, reduce cooling-related energy requirements and nearly eliminate cooling-related water consumption, depending on system design and operating conditions. The fluids also support recovery, reprocessing and reuse, enabling circularity. Chemours is collaborating with Oak Ridge National Laboratory, NTT DATA, 2CRSi, DataVolt, Munters, Accelsius and ZutaCore to accelerate the process. signal_briefs.raw_text: NATO Opens Counter-Drone Marketplace With 16 Systems From Five Companies - Inside Unmanned Systems On Nov. 5, NATO launched a Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-UAS) marketplace. Allies can buy pre-selected counter-drone solutions directly from a NATO catalog, with no further tender required. Image: NATO The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) competed and selected 16 solutions from five companies: Alta Ares, Axon Enterprise, Northrop Grumman, OSL UK and Quantum Systems. NATO said the selected capabilities have already been deployed in allied countries and in Ukraine. They include static, transportable and on-the-move systems. The marketplace is part of Drone Edge, an initiative launched at the NATO Summit Defence Industry Forum in Ankara in July. Under Drone Edge, allies committed to investing more than $40 billion in counter-drone capabilities over the next five years. NATO has also allocated €3.1 million to fund further testing of the selected systems by nations or NATO commands. Four Reference Scenarios NCIA evaluated bids against four reference scenarios. Area protection covers a zone up to 3 kilometers in diameter, such as an airbase or logistics hub. Border protection extends across a 20-kilometer border segment. Convoy protection covers a moving column up to 300 meters long traveling at up to 50 kilometers per hour. Point protection focuses on a single high-value asset or location, such as a command post. NCIA hosts the NATO Counter-UAS Centre of Expertise and manages the multi-award framework contracts, which are valid for 18 months. NATO intends to run regular competitions so that newer technologies reach allies. The frameworks are not purchase orders in themselves. Individual orders will be placed through subsequent contracts with the selected suppliers. The competition predates Drone Edge. signal_briefs.raw_text: What is immersion cooling for data centers? null Home Insights What is immersion cooling for data centers? What is immersion cooling for data centers? 8 min. Read 11/6/26 Rising AI rack densities are pushing traditional cooling approaches further. Immersion cooling brings liquid directly to IT equipment to manage higher heat loads. Immersion cooling for data centers is a liquid cooling method that replaces traditional IT equipment racks with sealed tanks or enclosures filled with thermally conductive dielectric fluid. Servers and other components are submerged in the fluid, which absorbs heat directly from hardware surfaces and transfers it away from the IT equipment. Data centers supporting AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads are key use cases for immersion cooling as rack densities increase. Immersion cooling can support higher heat loads and help reduce fan and facility energy use, but it can require significant equipment and operational changes within the data center. How immersion cooling works Immersion cooling submerges IT equipment in dielectric fluid, allowing the fluid to absorb heat directly from the components. The system then transfers that heat away from the IT equipment and ultimately to the facility cooling infrastructure. The way the fluid transfers and rejects heat depends on the type of immersion cooling system. The two primary approaches are single-phase and two-phase immersion cooling. Single-phase immersion cooling Immersion cooling involves placing IT equipment horizontally in a sealed tank that resembles a server rack on its back. Servers are inserted from the top and position them vertically in dielectric fluid. The fluid absorbs heat directly from the submerged IT components, reducing the number of heat-transfer steps compared with air cooling. (see Figure 1) Figure 1. In immersion cooling, dielectric fluids absorb heat from the IT equipment and transfer the heat to heat exchangers in coolant distribution units (CDUs) . Source
